title: When Warnings Are Taken as Jokes

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his daughters. He said, "Hurry and get out of this place, because the Lord is about to destroy the city!" But his sons-in-law thought he was joking. - Gen 19:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Lot rushes to warn his sons-in-law: "Hurry and get out! The Lord is about to destroy the city!" But they don't take him seriously. "His sons-in-law thought he was joking." The warning was real, the danger was hours away, and they laughed it off. Their disbelief would cost them everything.

This is a heartbreaking moment. Lot finally speaks a true and urgent word - and it lands on ears that will not hear. Part of the tragedy may be Lot's own compromised witness; a man known for going along with Sodom suddenly warning of Sodom's destruction was easy to dismiss. When our lives have not matched our words, people struggle to believe us when it matters most.

But the deeper tragedy is the human tendency to treat God's warnings as jokes. The message of coming judgement has always seemed absurd to those comfortable in their sin. In Noah's day, people ate and drank and laughed until the flood came (Matt 24:38-39). It is the same in every age.

There is a solemn lesson here, both for how we live and how we listen. May our lives lend weight to our words, so our witness is believable. And may we ourselves never treat God's warnings as jokes. The message of salvation in Christ is not a punchline; it is life and death. "How shall we escape if we ignore so great a salvation?" (Heb 2:3).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does your life lend weight to your words, or undermine them?
- Are there warnings from God you have been treating too lightly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, let my life lend weight to my witness, so my words are believed. And keep me from ever treating Your warnings as jokes. Help me take Your voice with the seriousness it deserves.
Amen.
